subject: Post-demo: model fit & quantization tradeoffs for AtlasRetail integration
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: model fit & quantization tradeoffs for AtlasRetail integration

Hi Simon / Dana —

Thanks again for taking the product demo today — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we heard:

1) Goals we heard from the call
- Improve in-app search and assisted merchandising copy (product titles, descriptions) with high precision for category / attribute extraction.
- Target throughput: ~5k inference requests/day today, with burst to 20k/day during promotions; latency target ~ <300ms p50 for the simple reranking flows.
- Quality constraints: <1% drop vs current baseline on key extraction accuracy; we prioritize precision over fluency for the extraction flows.

2) Initial model fit recommendations (based on quick evals we ran during the demo)
- Llama-2-13B-chat (quant-friendly variant): strong balance of quality and cost for structured extraction + templates.
- Llama-2-70B / 70B-chat (if you expect heavier contextual reasoning for merchandising rules) — better quality but higher compute.
- We can run smaller dedicated fine-tune/eval runs on your prompt set to confirm fit.

3) Quantization / throughput trade study (summary)
- AWQ (8-bit asymmetric) — best throughput uplift with relatively small quality delta on extraction tasks; recommended first pass if ~1–3% quality tolerance.
- GPTQ (4/8-bit variants) — generally preserves higher fidelity but depends on model architecture; longer conversion time but useful when quality SLOs are strict.
- FP8 / hardware FP8 paths — emerging, can give great density on compatible infra but currently more experimental and hardware-dependent.

I attached the prompt set we discussed (atlas_prompt_set_v1.json) and a quick benchmark PDF (redwood_benchmark_results_20260218.pdf) showing our baseline runs and the AWQ/GPTQ rows. I also attached a tradeoffs spreadsheet (quantization_tradeoffs_awq_gptq_fp8.xlsx) with latency, cost, and quality deltas from our lab. Links to the Drive eval folder are below.

Proposed next steps
- Redwood runs a focused POC: 2x prompt-set evals (13B quantized AWQ and 70B GPTQ baseline) + a follow-up report — target turnaround 5 business days.
- We'll include per-prompt quality deltas and per-token latency/cost estimates.
- Quick sync next Tue (2/24) to review results and decide whether to move to a short pilot (1–2 weeks).

Can you confirm POC scope and whether the throughput / latency targets above look right? If yes, I’ll kick off the evals and invite a short review meeting.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the detailed recap and attachments. A few quick clarifying questions before you kick off the POC:

1) Latency / infra: our production latency target is 300ms p50 for the simple extraction endpoint when serving ~5k/day. In your benchmark PDF the 13B AWQ p50 shows ~210ms on the GPU type you used — can you confirm the GPU instance type and whether those numbers assume multi-request batching or single-stream?

2) Quality sensitivity: we care a lot about precision on attribute extraction (SKU attribute mapping). You noted AWQ might incur 1–3% delta — can you confirm if that was evaluated on generative tasks vs structured extraction? For SKU mapping even a 1% drop is problematic.

3) Cost ballpark: any rough delta vs a FP16 13B baseline (per 1M tokens) so we can plan budget?

4) Timeline: 5 business days for the evals works for us if you can start Monday. Please include any short readme on how to interpret the per-prompt deltas.

Also looping in Dana (ops) who will validate latency requirements and confirm any infra constraints.

Simon
Head of Product, AtlasRetail

Hi Simon / Dana —

Thanks — great questions. Short answers below + details on what we'll run for the POC.

1) Benchmark infra / latency assumptions - The numbers in redwood_benchmark_results_20260218.pdf were collected on an NVIDIA A10G-equivalent instance with single-stream (no batching) latencies reported. The p50 ~210ms for 13B AWQ was single-stream, prompt length ~60 tokens. If you plan to run on different hardware (e.g., A100 or T4) we can re-run on your preferred SKU.

2) Quality sensitivity & measurement - The 1–3% delta was measured primarily on generative tasks — we included extraction-style prompts in the spreadsheet but will prioritize SKU/attribute mapping for your POC. For extraction tasks AWQ impact is often smaller, but because SKU mapping is high-sensitivity we will add strict per-attribute precision/recall checks and flag any prompt-level regressions >0.5%.

3) Cost ballpark - Roughly: AWQ 13B => ~45–55% of FP16 cost per-token in our infra (varies by GPU and batch). GPTQ 13B (higher-fidelity) sits closer to 60–75% of FP16 cost. 70B numbers scale proportionally and we'll include a per-1M-token estimate in the final POC report. We'll include a sensitivity table in the spreadsheet.

4) Timeline & deliverables - We'll start Monday (2/23) and deliver:
  - Per-prompt precision/recall table (CSV)
  - Per-model latency/cost estimates (spreadsheet tab)
  - Notes on any prompts with regression >0.5%
  - Recommendation: AWQ 13B for initial pilot, fallback to GPTQ 13B or 70B if we see regression on critical prompts

Internal note to Rishi: please prioritize SKU mapping evals and include side-by-side token-level diffs for prompts tagged {sku}. Run on an A100 if available and include single-stream + 8-concurrency simulated burst numbers.

Simon / Dana — can you confirm we should proceed with the scope above and whether you want us to run on A100 or the GPU type you plan to use for pilot? Also confirm any compliance/whitelisting needed to pull the prompt set from your S3.

Thanks,
Marissa
